LESSON: COMPUTER CONCEPTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Foundations of Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 1.3: Computer Concepts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Computer Concepts, part of Foundations of Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are computers classified differently? 2. How are computers used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the meaning of the terms; computer, data, and information,

2. discuss characteristics of a computer (speed, accuracy, versatility, reliability, diligence, storage, consistency),

3. download and watch a video clip on classification of computers,

4. discuss the classification of computers (functionality, purpose, and size) in a user environment,

5. interact with different types of computers in the user environment to perform tasks. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the meaning of the terms; computer, data, and information,
2. discuss characteristics of a computer (speed, accuracy, versatility, reliability, diligence, storage, consistency),
3. download and watch a video clip on classification of computers,
4. discuss the classification of computers (functionality, purpose, and size) in a user environment,
5. interact with different types of computers in the user environment to perform tasks. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Computer Concepts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops interpretation and inference skills while brainstorming on the

meaning of the terms; computer, data, and information.

• Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening, and teamwork skills when discussing the

classification of computers in a user environment.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner shows accountability by caring for the print or digital media when interacting with different types of

computers in the user environment to perform tasks.

• Peace: learner displays patience with peers when discussing the classification of computers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cyber Security: learner observes online safety when downloading and watching a video clip on classification of computers.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner is able to relate the skills of interacting with different types of computers to the use of a calculator in Mathematics.
